findings.claim: The supplied router and capability catalog agree on six admitted foundation procedures: identity.session, identity.scopes, identity.entry and identity.syncCredentials are queries; identity.createInitialBond and authority.refreshSnapshot are commands. Each is admitted for the app channel with session assurance and required G2 evidence. This declaration does not demonstrate that the evidence was achieved or that production execution works.

Every shown procedure passes through a guard requiring identity and platform. syncCredentials returns SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE when its issuer is absent. Security procedure implementations, actual authentication, database authority enforcement and failure handling beyond this router are not supplied.

The catalog description's unqualified empty v1 contract statement is inconsistent with the six present procedures. Its narrower empty business contract/router wording remains consistent with the supplied foundation-only router and deferred business admission. Preserve the historical reset context and warning that historical evidence does not establish current execution, while reviewing the current-state wording.

The governing policy's statement that current source has two read-only identity procedures needs review: the supplied router now has five identity procedures and one authority procedure, including two commands. This factual drift does not invalidate the policy's continuing horizontal-foundation scope or deferred business admission.

Resuming horizontal foundation work does not authorize implementing business procedures or inventing product policy. Existing foundation commands do not imply business admission. The authorized transport remains native oRPC v2 exclusively at /api/v1, without legacy aliases, converters or parallel first-party OpenAPI transport.
